title: Overdub: RPG Maker MZ Default Sound Replacement
shortText: 137 new sound effects named exactly like RPG Maker MZ's defaults. Copy one folder and the whole game sounds new.
html:
Every default sound a new MZ project plays, re-voiced

137 new sound effects, each named exactly like an RPG Maker MZ default sound effect. Back up your project's audio/se folder, copy Overdub's ogg folder over it, and every menu, battle, hit and spell in the default database plays the new set. No database edits. No plugin.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, free or paid, on any platform, including deployed RPG Maker games. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Every sound is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: the whole system and menu family, 9 files (Cursor3, Decision2, Cancel2, Buzzer1, Equip1, Save2, Load2, Shop1, Item3). Drop them into a test project's audio/se and move around the menus.

What gets replaced

A new MZ project's database plays 137 distinct sound effect names: the 24 system sound slots (23 files: cursor, OK, cancel, buzzer, save, load, battle start, escape, damage, collapse and the rest) and the 455 sound cues inside the 120 default animations. Overdub ships a new sound under every one of those names, read from the engine's own data files.

  • System and menu (9)
  • Battle flow (11)
  • Collapse (4)
  • Blows and impacts (8)
  • Blades and shots (15)
  • Fire (7)
  • Ice (6)
  • Thunder (9)
  • Water (5)
  • Earth (6)
  • Wind (7)
  • Light and healing (13)
  • Darkness and status (18)
  • Arcane (19)

One identity, all 137

Lantern bronze and glass in a stone hall. Every struck sound uses the same two materials, every impact lands on the same stone floor, the rest is shaped air and grit, and every sound is finished in the same hall. Menu cues, battle hits and spells sound like they come from one game.

Tested in the engine's own code

  • MZ's own runtime scripts played every system sound and every default animation cue (479 calls) from a project folder holding only Overdub's files: 137 names requested, 478 of 478 decoded on the browser path and 478 of 478 on the engine's own Vorbis decoder (the Safari and iOS path).
  • Encrypted deployment tested too: the files encrypted the way the MZ deployer writes them and loaded through the engine's own decryption, 956 of 956 requests served encrypted and every name decoded.
  • 58 cues are checked for the shape of their job: menu ticks short and immediate, swings that arrive on their frame, hits at full level at once, charges that build.
  • The inner 80% of the pack sits within 0.63 dB (median -20.37 dBFS), so the database's default volume works for a cursor tick and a thunderclap alike.
  • 1241 signal checks passed, 0 failed: no clipping, no silence, no abrupt starts or ends, lengths in band.

Things worth knowing

  • Only the 137 names a new project uses are replaced. Default names your own events or plugins use keep playing their originals; MANIFEST.md lists every name and where the default database uses it.
  • The default animations play 319 of their 455 cues at a pitch other than 100 (from 50 to 150); the engine transposes these files exactly as it transposed the defaults.
  • To restore the defaults, copy your backup back over audio/se.

What is in the zip

  • 137 OGG files to copy into audio/se, plus the same 137 sounds as WAV (44.1 kHz, 16 bit, mono) for editing.
  • MANIFEST.md, Readme_for_Users.md with the drop in and restore steps, LICENSE.txt, pack.json.

More sound from the studio

  • Blip: Dialogue Voices for Text Advance: character voice blips for message windows, the text advance sound MZ does not ship.
  • Akatsuki: Anime / JRPG Sound Suite: a JRPG sound suite struck from bronze, glass, bamboo and steel, for projects that want new cues under their own names.
  • Sixfold: Elemental Casting Chains: six elements, each with the same twelve stage casting chain, for custom skill animations.

How it was made

Every sound was made from scratch by a program. No audio from RPG Maker or any other source was used; only the file names match, so the engine finds them. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the makers of RPG Maker. The code that generates the sounds was written with AI assistance; no generative audio model was used. The store images are drawn by a program from the shipped files, and the cover illustration is AI generated.
